cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:16 — *In that I command thee this day to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it.* *Walk then in these my commandments, and ye shall live unto Elohim (God).* (Hermas 23:1) The angel's call to walk in the commandments and live has the shape of the word Moses set before Yashar'el (Israel) at the border of the land: love Yahuah (God), walk in his ways, keep his commandments, and live. The scripture stands first, and the line in the Shepherd sounds beside it.
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 30:16 — *to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply* Walk in the commandments and live, as it was first set before Yashar'el.

cards.note: 1 Timothy 5:6 — *But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth.* *In these, therefore, there is not repentance unto life. For the Name of Elohim (God) is being blasphemed through them. The life of such persons is death.* (Hermas 23:2) Paul's one line about the widow who lives in pleasure says plainly what the Shepherd's angel says at length: a life given over to its appetites is a death already under way.
cards.member_note: 1 Timothy 5:6 — *But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth.* A life given over to pleasure is already death.

cards.note: Psalm 119:71 — *It is good for me that I have been afflicted; that I might learn thy statutes.* *When then they are afflicted with every kind of affliction, then they are delivered over to me for good instruction, and are strengthened in the faith of Yahuah (Lord), and serve Yahuah (Lord) with a pure heart the remaining days of their life.* (Hermas 23:3) The psalmist found that affliction taught him the statutes of Yahuah (God), and the Shepherd's angel of punishment is likewise said to deliver men to good instruction so that they return to serve Yahuah (God) with a pure heart. The psalm names what the instruction is for: to learn his statutes.
cards.member_note: Psalm 119:71 — *It is good for me that I have been afflicted; that I might learn thy statutes.* Affliction that teaches the statutes of Yahuah.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:25 — *Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of Elohim (God), than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;* *the time of the self-indulgence and deceit is very short, but the time of the punishment and torment is long.* (Hermas 23:4) Moses is spoken of as choosing affliction with the people of Elohim (God) over the pleasures of sin, which last only for a season. Scripture gives no reckoning of hours and years, but it agrees with the Shepherd that the pleasure is brief and that the choice lies between it and the people of Elohim (God).
cards.member_note: Hebrews 11:25 — *Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of Elohim (God), than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season* The pleasures of sin last only for a season.

thread.title: The pleasure that ends in death, and the instruction that brings back
thread.summary_md:
Hermas hears the angel call him to the commandments: *Walk then in these my commandments, and ye shall live unto Elohim (God).* (Hermas 23:1) Then he is shown two shepherds, one who feeds men on their appetites and one who punishes, and told of the first: *The life of such persons is death.* (Hermas 23:2)

It ain't new. Moses had put the same choice before Yashar'el (Israel): *In that I command thee this day to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it.* (Deuteronomy 30:16) And the word that there is a way of living that is already dying is in Paul's line about the widow: *But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth.* (1 Timothy 5:6)

The angel says that the afflicted are handed over to instruction: *they are delivered over to me for good instruction, and are strengthened in the faith of Yahuah (Lord)* (Hermas 23:3) The psalmist says the same from the inside of it: *It is good for me that I have been afflicted; that I might learn thy statutes.* (Psalm 119:71) And when the angel says the season of self-indulgence is short beside the torment that follows, *the time of the self-indulgence and deceit is very short, but the time of the punishment and torment is long.* (Hermas 23:4) the writer to the Hebrews calls it a season too: *Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of Elohim (God), than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;* (Hebrews 11:25)

The Shepherd closes the chapter with a warning that those who stay in their pleasures and do not repent bring death upon themselves, *and if they continue in them and repent not, they bring death upon themselves.* (Hermas 23:5) which is the choice of life and death that Moses set before the people, *therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.* (Deuteronomy 30:19)

chapters.flag: Hermas verses 23:1-23:5 are each a single very long paragraph, so each card quotes one contiguous sentence run from the verse (verbatim, checked by script) and not the whole verse. The hours-and-days reckoning of torment in 23:4 and the two angels are not endorsed; the notes set scripture beside the lines only.

cards.note: Psalm 51:17 — *The sacrifices of Elohim (God) are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise.* *and if he endure the afflictions which come upon him, assuredly He Who created all things and endowed them with power will be moved with compassion and will bestow some remedy. And this (will Elohim (God) do), if in any way He perceive the heart of the penitent pure from every evil thing.* (Hermas 24:1) The Shepherd speaks of the penitent who humbles himself in every action and endures, until Elohim (God) sees a heart pure and is moved with compassion. The psalm names what Elohim (God) will not despise: a broken and a contrite heart.
cards.member_note: Psalm 51:17 — *a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise.* Elohim does not despise a broken and contrite heart.

cards.note: Leviticus 26:3 — *If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them;* *And if thou keep these commandments with thy household, all affliction shall hold aloof from thee; yea, and affliction," saith he, "shall hold aloof from all whosoever shall walk in these my commandments.* (Hermas 24:1) The Shepherd's promise that affliction will hold aloof from those who walk in his commandments is the old shape of the covenant. Whatever commandments the angel has in view, the covenant word that sets the blessing before those who walk in the commandments and do them was spoken by Yahuah (God) to Yashar'el (Israel), and this is its opening.
cards.member_note: Leviticus 26:3 — *If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them;* The covenant word on walking in the commandments and doing them, with its blessing to follow.

thread.title: The head of the house is afflicted, and the household repents
thread.summary_md:
The angel tells Hermas that his house must be afflicted for a time, and that repentance is not a single moment: *and if he endure the afflictions which come upon him, assuredly He Who created all things and endowed them with power will be moved with compassion and will bestow some remedy. And this (will Elohim (God) do), if in any way He perceive the heart of the penitent pure from every evil thing.* (Hermas 24:1)

It ain't new that the way back runs through humility. *The sacrifices of Elohim (God) are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise.* (Psalm 51:17) Yet scripture also shows mercy and consequence standing together in one place. When David confessed, the answer came at once: *And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against Yahuah (LORD). And Nathan said unto David, Yahuah (LORD) also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.* (2 Samuel 12:13) And the consequence still followed: *Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of Yahuah (LORD) to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.* (2 Samuel 12:14) The forgiveness was real, and so was the affliction that the deed had set in motion.

The angel ends by telling the head of the house that if he keeps the commandments with his household affliction will keep away: *And if thou keep these commandments with thy household, all affliction shall hold aloof from thee; yea, and affliction," saith he, "shall hold aloof from all whosoever shall walk in these my commandments.* (Hermas 24:1) Yahuah (God) had already set that condition before Yashar'el (Israel), with its blessing to follow: *If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them;* (Leviticus 26:3)

The household bears what its head bears, and the way home is through a pure heart and a walk in the commandments. Scripture holds both the mercy and the cost in the same hand, and the Shepherd's lines are read beside it.

chapters.flag: Hermas 24:1 is one very long verse; each card quotes a verbatim contiguous excerpt, not the whole verse. The angel's line that the sins of the repentant are not 'forgiven forthwith' is not endorsed or attacked; the thread sets Nathan's word to David (2 Samuel 12:13-14) beside it so the reader sees forgiveness and consequence together.
